correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact six nonconstant forbidden length-three patterns 001,011,100,110,010,101; for a,b>=3, 000 and 111 necessarily appear. Each avoidance class is a unique word at its permitted c: low/high c intervals for four patterns and divisibility a|c,b|c for the two single-contiguous-block patterns. Two endpoint words have multiplicity four, accounting for subtracting three each, and six further pairwise junction coincidences have to be subtracted once each (including when c labels coincide for a=b); no other run forms overlap. The Gaussian binomial counts every (a,b,c) fiber. The collision classification gives bound R<=2 and total 3(a+b)-6 by counting six families and subtracting 12 duplicates. New independent source-code-independent enumeration selected all b-one position subsets, counted scattered 01 directly and generated length-three subsequences via all triples of indices for 22,460 words across 33 (a,b) cases with 3<=a,b<=8, a+b<=14: every R and bound matched. Finite checks do not prove all a,b; run-form classification does.

originality.rationale: Fazekas–Huang–Mercaş (2026) characterize whether every member of a fixed Parikh-matrix language is three-universal, via the same six avoidance CONDITIONS. Their criterion does not count all failing words per fixed fiber or give the 0/1/2 correction, overlap multiplicities or total. The published full length-only universality-index law likewise cannot recover the conditional three-parameter distribution. An implicit enumeration from older run-classification literature remains a priority risk.

final_claim: For a,b>=3 and 0<=c<=ab, binary words having a zeros, b ones and c scattered 01 occurrences have U_{a,b}(c)=P_{a,b}(c)-R_{a,b}(c) three-subsequence-universal members, with P the c-th coefficient of the Gaussian binomial (a+b choose a)_t and R the explicit six-avoidance-family indicator/inclusion-exclusion correction in RESULT.md. Every R is 0,1,2 and sum_{c=0}^{ab}R=3(a+b)-6.
